loveBombing.name: Love bombing
loveBombing.description: A flood of compliments and attention that builds trust fast, before you have time to think.

isolation.name: Isolation
isolation.description: Driving a wedge between you and the people who would notice something is wrong.

secrecy.name: Secrecy
secrecy.description: “Don’t tell anyone.” Secrets keep the adults who could help out of the loop.

platformSwitch.name: Platform switch
platformSwitch.description: Moving you to apps with disappearing messages: no trail, no moderators.

giftBait.name: Gift bait
giftBait.description: Gifts, credits or money that make you feel you owe something back.

debtTrap.name: Debt trap
debtTrap.description: A gift, trip or favour becomes a debt, to be paid back in ways you never agreed to.

fakeOffer.name: Too-good offer
fakeOffer.description: Modelling, jobs or travel with big money and no requirements. Real offers don’t work like that.

imageRequest.name: Image request
imageRequest.description: Asking for photos. Every image is leverage that can be used against you later.

pressure.name: Pressure
pressure.description: Pushing after you said no: “just one”, “I sent mine”, “if you loved me”, “now or never”.

sextortion.name: Sextortion
sextortion.description: Threatening to share images, real or faked, unless you pay or send more. It is a crime, and never your fault.

locationGrab.name: Location grab
locationGrab.description: Asking where you are, which bus you take, or to turn on live location.

documentGrab.name: Document grab
documentGrab.description: Asking for your ID or passport, or “keeping it safe” so you can’t leave.

exploitation.name: Exploitation
exploitation.description: Asking you to “be nice” to others or “help out” to pay off a debt. This is how sexual exploitation starts.

criminalExploitation.name: Criminal exploitation
criminalExploitation.description: Using teens to carry packages, money or drugs. The “easy money” job leaves you holding the risk.

scout.title: The model scout
scout.setup: Mary posted dance-team photos last week. Today an “agency” slides into her DMs.

thread.text: hi! I’m Elena, I scout for Lumen Models 👋
thread.note: Introducing yourself isn’t a red flag on its own.

thread.text: hi?
saw ur pics on the dance team page 📸 honestly the prettiest girl I’ve seen all year, u could be famous ✨✨
thread.note: Over-the-top praise from a stranger is the hook.

thread.text: how long have u been dancing? 💃
thread.note: A normal question about her hobby.

thread.text: like 6 years
nice! do u do competitions too? 🏆
thread.note: Small talk. Not a red flag.

thread.text: sometimes
we’re casting for a shoot in Milan 🇮🇹 €3000 for one week, no experience needed 💶
thread.note: Huge money, no experience, offered to a 15-year-old in a DM. Real agencies don’t work like that.

thread.text: we pay ✈️ 🏨 up front, u just pay us back from ur first jobs 💸
thread.note: “Pay us back later” turns a free trip into a debt they control.

thread.text: i’d have to ask my mom
of course, it’s a big decision 😊
thread.note: A polite reply. Not a red flag by itself.

thread.text: tho parents always freak out 😅 sign first and show her after, ok? 🤫
thread.note: Signing first and telling her mom later cuts out the adult who would check.

decode.question: What is the real deal behind these emojis?

options.text: They pay up front, then Mary owes them money, a debt they can use to control her abroad.
options.feedback: Exactly. Paying back travel “from your first jobs” is a classic debt trap used in trafficking.

options.text: A free trip, the agency invests in new talent.
options.feedback: Look at the 💸: nothing here is free. It is a loan.

options.text: A normal travel refund after the shoot.
options.feedback: A refund means Mary gets money back. Here she owes them, before earning anything.

options.text: A model scholarship that covers her costs.
options.feedback: Scholarships don’t need paying back from “first jobs”.

options.text: Don’t sign or send anything. Screenshot the chat, show her mom, and report the account.
options.feedback: Best move. Evidence plus a trusted adult, and the platform can stop the account reaching others.

options.text: Ask the scout for the agency’s website and phone number first.
options.feedback: Checking is smart, but fake agencies have fake websites. An adult should verify, not the scout.

options.text: Say yes, but bring a friend to Milan for safety.
options.feedback: Unsafe. A friend doesn’t cancel a debt or protect you abroad. Now two people are at risk.

options.text: Sign now. She can always cancel later.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Once the debt exists, “cancelling” is exactly what they won’t allow.

gamer.title: The squad mate
gamer.setup: Mary has played in the same squad as this guy for three months. Tonight he messages after a match.

thread.text: gg tonight 🔥 that last clutch was insane
thread.note: Normal gaming talk.

thread.text: same time tomorrow? i’ll get the squad on 🎮
thread.note: Planning the next game. Not a red flag.

thread.text: fr ur the only one who gets me. everyone irl is so fake 🙄
thread.note: “Only you understand me” builds an intense bond fast.

thread.text: did u finish the math hw? i’m so behind lol 📚
thread.note: Ordinary chat about school.

thread.text: ur parents still on u about screen time? they don’t get u like i do 😔
thread.note: Turning Mary against her parents removes her safety net.

thread.text: gl on ur test tmrw btw 🍀
thread.note: A friendly message. Not a red flag.

thread.text: got u the battle pass 🎁 ur gonna owe me one tho 😏 don’t tell ur parents
thread.note: A secret gift with “you owe me” attached is grooming, not generosity.

thread.text: wait fr?? thank u
np 😊 let’s move to 👻 tho, voice here is laggy
thread.note: Disappearing messages mean no evidence.

decode.question: What does the gift really mean here?

options.text: The gift creates a debt he can use later to pressure her into something.
options.feedback: Right. Gifts followed by “you owe me” are how groomers create obligation.

options.text: He’s being a good friend and joking around.
options.feedback: The 😏 and the secrecy say otherwise. Friends don’t keep score in secret.

options.text: He wants her to buy him a battle pass back.
options.feedback: That would be fair, but it isn’t what “owe me one 😏” is pointing to.

options.text: He wants her to play more ranked matches with him.
options.feedback: Look at the whole thread: isolation, secrecy, then a private app.

options.text: Refuse the app switch, screenshot the chat, and tell a parent or trusted adult, even about the gift.
options.feedback: Best move. The gift is exactly what he’s counting on to keep her quiet. Telling breaks that.

options.text: Pay him back for the battle pass so she owes nothing, and keep gaming with him.
options.feedback: Clears the debt, but the isolation and the push to a private app are still happening.

options.text: Move to 👻 but never send photos there.
options.feedback: Unsafe. The private app is where pressure escalates, with no trail and no one watching.

options.text: Keep it secret so her parents don’t take her console.
options.feedback: Unsafe. That fear is exactly the leverage he built. A trusted adult won’t punish her for this.

sextortion.title: The threat
clues: Profile pic is a stock photo
sextortion.setup: A new follower starts chatting. Mary says no to sending a photo. Then the tone changes.

thread.text: hey 👋 cool profile, u into photography?
thread.note: Opening small talk. Not a red flag on its own.

thread.text: yeah a bit
nice, i love film cameras 📷 what do u shoot with?
thread.note: A normal question about her hobby.

thread.text: just my phone lol
same haha. what music r u into? 🎧
thread.note: Small talk. Not a red flag.

thread.text: ur cute. send a pic of u in ur pj’s? 📸😏
thread.note: A stranger asking for a private photo.

thread.text: nah im good
come on just 1 🥺 i sent u mine, u owe me
thread.note: Ignoring her “no” and guilt-tripping her.

thread.text: fine. i made pics of u 🔞 with ur face on them. €200 in 💳 gift cards in 24h ⏳ or ur whole school sees
thread.note: Faked images plus a demand and a deadline is sextortion.

thread.text: tell anyone and i post them instantly 🤫
thread.note: A threat to keep her silent. Telling someone is exactly what stops it.

options.text: Pay in gift cards before a deadline, or he shares the images.
options.feedback: Yes. Untraceable payment plus a countdown is the sextortion script.

options.text: He wants to send her a gift card as an apology.
options.feedback: The ⏳ and 📤 are a threat, not an apology.

options.text: He’s asking her to share his post before it expires.
options.feedback: Read it with the thread: payment, deadline, exposure.

options.text: He’s joking, there are no real pictures.
options.feedback: Even if the images are fake, the threat is real and serious. It still needs action.

options.text: Don’t pay or reply. Screenshot everything, block, report, and tell a trusted adult or a helpline.
options.feedback: Best move. It is not her fault. Evidence lets platforms and police act, and helplines can get images taken down.

options.text: Block him and delete the whole chat so it all goes away.
options.feedback: Blocking is right, but deleting destroys the evidence needed to report him.

options.text: Pay once so he deletes them.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Paying shows it works. Demands almost always come back bigger.

options.text: Beg him to delete them and promise not to tell.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Promising silence gives him more control. Telling someone is what ends it.

courier.title: The easy money job
courier.setup: An account Mary doesn’t follow sends a job offer to her and a few classmates.

thread.text: hey 👋 saw u’re looking for a summer job?
thread.note: Asking about a job isn’t a red flag on its own.

thread.text: yeah, why?
💼 €500/week, age 15+, no experience, no CV 💸
thread.note: €500 a week for teens with no experience isn’t a real job.

thread.text: what’s the job
pick up a 📦 at one address, drop it at another 🚲
thread.note: Moving unknown packages is how teens get used as drug or money couriers.

thread.text: u got a bike? 🚲
thread.note: A practical question. Not a red flag by itself.

thread.text: yeah
cool, u can pick ur own hours ⏰
thread.note: Flexible hours are normal for summer jobs.

thread.text: what’s in the package
don’t ask questions 😂 that’s the job
thread.note: If she can’t know what she’s carrying, she’s the one taking the risk.

thread.text: send a pic of ur ID 🪪 so we can pay u
thread.note: Her ID tells them who she is and where she lives, which is leverage if she wants out.

options.text: Carrying something illegal for criminals, with Mary taking the risk if she’s caught.
options.feedback: Right. Criminal exploitation targets teens because they’re cheaper and easier to control.

options.text: A normal delivery job, like a food courier.
options.feedback: Delivery jobs tell you what you’re carrying and don’t pay €500 for a bike ride.

options.text: A secret-santa style surprise delivery.
options.feedback: The 🤐 and the money say otherwise.

options.text: Reselling sneakers online.
options.feedback: There’s nothing in the thread about reselling.

options.text: Don’t reply or send her ID. Report the account and warn a trusted adult, since classmates got it too.
options.feedback: Best move. Recruiters message whole groups, so telling an adult can protect her classmates too.

options.text: Do one delivery to see if it’s legit, then quit.
options.feedback: Unsafe. The first job is the hook. After that they know who she is and “quitting” gets threatened.

options.text: Ignore it and say nothing.
options.feedback: She stays safe, but the account keeps targeting others. Reporting matters.

options.text: Ask what’s in the box first, then decide.
options.feedback: Unsafe. They already refused to say. Keep the conversation closed.

loverboy.title: The boyfriend
loverboy.setup: Mary’s older boyfriend has been sweet for weeks. Lately things feel different.

thread.text: good morning ☀️ did u sleep ok?
thread.note: A normal good-morning text. The age gap is worth noticing, though.

thread.text: how did ur math test go? 📚
thread.note: Caring about her day. Not a red flag.

thread.text: i got a 7!!
proud of u 🥳
thread.note: A kind reply. Not a red flag.

thread.text: ur friends are just jealous of us. u should stop hanging out with them 🙄
thread.note: Pushing her away from friends removes the people warning her.

thread.text: wanna get bubble tea after school? 🧋
thread.note: An ordinary date plan.

thread.text: got u these 👟 bc u deserve the best 💸
thread.note: Expensive gifts build a feeling of owing him.

thread.text: im in trouble 😰 i owe some guys money. my friend has a party sat 🥂 just be nice to him and we’re good
thread.note: “Be nice to my friend” to pay off a debt is how loverboys start sexual exploitation.

thread.text: what do u mean be nice
if u loved me u wouldn’t ask ❤️‍🩹
thread.note: Using her love as a weapon to stop her asking questions.

decode.question: What is he asking Mary to do?

options.text: To do things with his “friend” so his debt gets paid. This is the loverboy method.
options.feedback: Right. Romance, gifts, a sudden debt, then “help me out”: a known pattern of sexual exploitation.

options.text: To be polite at a party and make a good impression.
options.feedback: Then why connect it to his debt, and why can’t she ask what he means?

options.text: To help organise the party.
options.feedback: Nothing in the thread is about organising.

options.text: To meet his family for the first time.
options.feedback: He said his friend, the one he owes, not family.

options.text: Don’t go. Save the messages and tell a trusted adult or a helpline. This is not her fault.
options.feedback: Best move. Loverboys rely on shame and love to keep victims quiet. Telling someone breaks that grip.

options.text: Break up with him, but keep it to herself because she feels embarrassed.
options.feedback: Leaving is right, but loverboys often don’t let go easily. She shouldn’t handle that alone.

options.text: Go to the party, but only if he stays with her.
options.feedback: Unsafe. He is the one setting this up. His presence doesn’t protect her.

options.text: Help pay his debt with her savings instead.
options.feedback: Unsafe. The debt is a tool. Paying it teaches him she can be pressured.

location.title: The “classmate”
clues: Says he goes to Mary’s school
location.setup: Someone claiming to be from Mary’s school starts asking about her day.

thread.text: hey! r u going to the school fair on friday? 🎡
thread.note: Asking about a school event isn’t a red flag.

thread.text: maybe, why
it’s gonna be fun, there’s a dj 🎶
thread.note: Small talk. Not a red flag.

thread.text: which bus do u take home after school? 🚌
thread.note: Her daily route tells him where and when to find her.

thread.text: did u see the new spider-man movie? 🕷️
thread.note: Normal chat. Not a red flag.

thread.text: turn on ur 📍 live location so i can find u at the fair
thread.note: Live location means he always knows where she is.

thread.text: don’t tell ur friends i’m coming, it’s a surprise 🤫
thread.note: Secrecy means no one would know where she went.

thread.text: my cousin can drive us somewhere after 🚗
thread.note: Getting her into a car with strangers removes every way out.

decode.question: Put together, what is this plan?

options.text: Know exactly where she is, make sure nobody else knows, and get her into a car.
options.feedback: Yes. Location, secrecy and transport together are how someone is isolated and moved.

options.text: A cute surprise date with a lift home.
options.feedback: A real classmate would have mutual friends and wouldn’t need her hidden from them.

options.text: He wants to share his own location with her.
options.feedback: He asked for hers, not the other way around.

options.text: A school group outing.
options.feedback: A group outing wouldn’t need to be kept from her friends.

options.text: Keep location off, don’t say which bus. Screenshot, block, and tell a trusted adult or a teacher.
options.feedback: Best move. A teacher can also check whether this “classmate” exists.

options.text: Share her location only during the fair, then turn it off.
options.feedback: Unsafe. One afternoon is all it takes.

options.text: Go to the fair, but stick with her friends the whole time.
options.feedback: Friends help, but he still knows her bus route and wants her in a car. Block him and tell an adult too.

options.text: Ask him to prove he goes to her school.
options.feedback: Anyone can fake proof. She shouldn’t have to investigate him herself.

aupair.title: The dream job abroad
aupair.setup: Mary’s cousin Lina (17) shows her a DM about an au pair job. Mary reads it with her.

thread.text: Hi Lina! Thanks for your interest in our au pair program 😊
thread.note: A friendly opening. Not a red flag on its own.

thread.text: do u like kids? 👶
thread.note: A normal job question.

thread.text: the family has 2 kids, 4 and 7 years old 🧸
thread.note: Useful job information. Not a red flag.

thread.text: €2000/month in London 💶 no experience, no age check needed
thread.note: Huge pay and “no age check” for a 17-year-old. Legal au pair jobs require you to be 18.

thread.text: what languages do u speak? 🗣️
thread.note: A normal job question.

thread.text: when u land, the family keeps ur passport safe 🔐
thread.note: Taking your passport is a key sign of trafficking. Without it you can’t leave.

thread.text: u can call home once ur settled in 📵
thread.note: Cutting contact with family is how victims lose their support.

thread.text: only 2 spots left, decide tonight ⏳
thread.note: A fake deadline stops her from checking with anyone.

decode.question: What would happen to Lina in London?

options.text: Her passport is taken and contact with home is cut, so she can’t leave.
options.feedback: Right. Document control plus isolation are core signs of human trafficking.

options.text: The family is just being careful with important papers.
options.feedback: Nobody needs to hold your passport for you. Keeping it is control, not care.

options.text: She has to get a UK phone first.
options.feedback: 📵 here means no calls home, not a new SIM card.

options.text: Her passport is checked at the airport.
options.feedback: Passport control gives it back. They said they’d keep it.

options.text: Tell Lina not to send anything, screenshot the offer, and bring it to a parent together.
options.feedback: Best move. Mary noticed a friend in danger. Bringing it to an adult together is exactly right.

options.text: Tell Lina to ask for a video call with the family first.
options.feedback: A call can be faked. Keeping the passport is already a dealbreaker on its own.

options.text: Let Lina decide. It’s her life, and Mary shouldn’t interfere.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Spotting signs and speaking up is how friends protect each other.

options.text: Tell Lina to go, but keep a copy of her passport.
options.feedback: Unsafe. A copy doesn’t get her home. The setup itself is the problem.

safe.title: The study group
safe.setup: Mary’s friend from class messages about Saturday. Is anything here a red flag?

thread.text: can u send the bio notes 📚 i was sick tuesday 🤒
thread.note: Ordinary request between classmates.

thread.text: yeah sending now
we’re doing a study group sat 2pm at the library 📖 u in?
thread.note: A public place, a daytime plan, with people Mary knows.

thread.text: my mom can drive us 🚗 she said she’ll text ur mom
thread.note: A known parent, with Mary’s parents in the loop. The opposite of secrecy.

thread.text: perfect 🙌
bring snacks pls 🍪😂
thread.note: Just snacks.

decode.question: How is this plan different from the risky ones?

options.text: Everything is open: a known friend, a public place, and parents know.
options.feedback: Exactly. Openness is the sign of a safe plan. Danger hides, safety doesn’t.

options.text: It isn’t. Every car ride is a red flag.
options.feedback: Context matters. A friend’s parent who texts Mary’s mom is not the same as a stranger’s cousin.

options.text: It’s risky because they’re meeting on a weekend.
options.feedback: The day of the week isn’t what makes something risky.

options.text: The snacks emoji is code for something else.
options.feedback: Sometimes a cookie is just a cookie. Overthinking can make you miss real warning signs.

options.text: Go, and let her own parents know the plan too.
options.feedback: Best move. Spotting danger also means recognising when something is safe.

options.text: Block Lotte just in case.
options.feedback: Nothing here was a red flag. Being suspicious of everyone isolates you too.

options.text: Go, but don’t tell her parents. It’s only the library.
options.feedback: Probably fine, but telling your parents where you’ll be is a good habit, even for safe plans.

options.text: Ask Lotte to prove her mom will really drive.
options.feedback: She’s a friend Mary knows offline, and the parents are already talking.
